summary: Implemented all 19 lifecycle-uc4-uc5 endpoints (AI Clause Analysis + Negotiation & Routing) against the 10 contract tables, with role enforcement, the UC4 risk/mandatory-clause/audit rules, and the UC5 routing/versioning/OTP-external-party flow. 35 new tests pass alongside the existing 132 (167 total); python -m compileall and pytest -q are clean. The server was booted on port 5199 and its OpenAPI document confirmed all 19 routes with the correct methods; role-based 401/403 were verified live. Full DB-backed happy paths were exercised via the in-memory SQLite test suite only, since no reachable Postgres instance exists in this sandbox (same limitation test_persistence.py already documents).

pr.title: feat(lifecycle-uc4-uc5): AI Clause Analysis + Negotiation & Routing API
pr.body: Implements all 19 endpoints of the lifecycle-uc4-uc5 module: AI Clause Analysis (clause review/accept/edit/reject, contract metadata, Ask AI, Proceed to Negotiation, audit log) and Negotiation & Routing (routing, tracker, reviewer submissions, OTP-secured external party flow, Compare Versions, reminders, Mark Agreed, comments). See this task's `blockers` for judgement calls made where the real AI pipeline, an email service, or a background scheduler is absent from this sandbox.

blockers: Task ownership conflict: a separate task file, .api-gen/tasks/T-LIFECYCLE-NEGOTIATION-API/TASK.md, claims ownership of the same two paths this task's own TASK.md assigns to me -- POST /api/v1/lifecycle/negotiation/external/{linkToken}/verify-otp and .../submit -- but with auth_required=no instead of this task's auth_required=yes for the same paths. I implemented both endpoints under this task (T-LIFECYCLE-CONTRACTS-API) exactly as its own endpoint table specifies (EXTERNAL_PARTY role, auth required), since that is the contract this task names as mine. If T-LIFECYCLE-NEGOTIATION-API is also run, its generator must not re-create these two routes/services or the app will have duplicate route registrations.

No real AI/document-parsing pipeline exists in this sandbox. 'AI Clause Analysis' is simulated: the first time a contract's clause-analysis is opened, every mandatory Active clause category from the tenant's UC123 clause library that is not yet represented is seeded as a Missing clause (risk_score=High, no suggested text), and a blank 'AI-suggested'-labelled contract_metadata row is created. Clauses whose library match is Standard/Deviated/Non-standard with real suggested text/AI explanations are never fabricated, since there is no document text to analyze; Accept Suggestion is therefore only reachable once a future task supplies that content. Ask AI's answer is a templated summary referencing the current overall risk score rather than a real LLM call.

UC4-AF-001's file-format check can only inspect the contract's Third Party Paper upload (the one uploaded-document reference this contract model carries) -- a contract built from a Template has no uploaded document for this module to validate, so it is always treated as a supported format.

UC4-BR-016 (re-flag Accepted/Edited clauses to Re-flagged after a tenant clause-library update) is not implemented: there is no trigger/event mechanism connecting UC123 clause-library edits to already-extracted contract_clauses rows in this codebase, and building one is out of this task's scope (clause library mutation endpoints belong to the uc123 module).

UC5-BR-001/002's mandatory-reviewer auto-add (Finance Head above INR 10,00,000; Legal Reviewer for High Risk contracts) adds a reviewer by name/role label when no matching user is already in the selected reviewer list; since 'Finance Head' is not one of this contract's five permitted X-User-Role values, there is no guaranteed real user to attach, so a synthetic reviewer_id is generated (negotiation_reviewers.reviewer_id has no FK constraint in the table contract, so this is schema-legal).

GenerateExternalLinkResponse gained one field not in context.json: `otp` (optional string). There is no email-sending infrastructure anywhere in this codebase to deliver UC5-BR-016's OTP to the External Party's inbox, so the OTP is returned directly in this response as the only way to drive the verify/submit flow end-to-end; `otp_hash` is still the persisted, compared value.

GET .../negotiation/compare has no request DTO in context.json (its endpoint entry is '-'), but UC5-FV-002/BR-012 require two prior version numbers as input. Added two required query parameters, `versionA` and `versionB` (integers), rather than inventing a request body DTO the contract never named.

Automatic daily overdue-reviewer reminders (UC5-AF-006/BR-010) are not implemented: there is no background scheduler/cron mechanism anywhere in this codebase to run a recurring job. Only the manual 'Send Reminder' endpoint (negotiation_reminders rows, reminder_type='Manual') is implemented.

UC5-AF-001/FV-001 describe blocking routing submission when neither a reviewer nor an external party is supplied, but RoutingRequest's externalPartyName/externalPartyEmail are typed as required (non-optional) strings in context.json, not optional alternatives to reviewer selection. Kept the contract's required-string typing and enforced 'at least one internal reviewer' as the AF-001/FV-001 validation instead of an OR-with-external-party check, since the DTO shape already makes the external party mandatory on every routing call.

Sequential/Parallel reviewer notification (UC5-BR-003/004) and the OTP email/secure-link delivery to the External Party are simulated via persisted state only (review_status, sequence_order, negotiation_external_links) -- no email/notification service exists in this codebase to actually dispatch anything.

UC5-BR-006 (triggering AI clause analysis automatically on an External Party's submitted redlines) is not implemented beyond persisting the new version/status transition, for the same reason noted above: there is no real AI pipeline in this sandbox to re-run.
